- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75–80), model overreacts; adjust downward by 3–8% for next 3–7 days.  
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting; delay forecast upward by 1–2 days if sentiment turns positive.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mid-term trends; apply 5–10% downward bias if sentiment remains negative or market shows consolidation.
